newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: New Nicaraguan government gets $27.5 mln from EU.
newsitem.headline: New Nicaraguan government gets $27.5 mln from EU.

text.p: The European Union (EU) has signed two contracts to provide Nicaragua with $27.5 million to bolster its education and judicial systems, Nicaragua's newly inaugurated government said on Sunday.
The EU will give $20.6 million to build schools and sporting centers in rural areas, and provide housing and training for teachers in the countryside, a government press release said.
"For us the education system is important because it is an investment in capital and with this support we will help our rural teachers," Nicaraguan President Arnoldo Aleman said.
The remaining $6.9 million will be used to modernize Nicaragua's judicial system, training judges and building courthouses across the country, the press release said.
Aleman has said his government, which took power on Friday, will make rebuilding Nicaragua's shaky judicial system and pauperized schools among its top priorities.
